clue.text: Top part of tree magnificent, as Walton noted in March

parts.note: the crown of a tree is its upper spread of branches
imperial means grand, majestic, fit for an emperor

explanation.surface: Admiring a splendid treetop and a stately piece of music in the same breath.
explanation.walkthrough: William Walton, the English composer, wrote a coronation march with this title in 1937, so 'noted in March' means set to music as a march.
explanation.definitionFit: Walton's 1937 coronation march for George VI bears this title.

clue.text: Holiday with girl for a song at the year-end

parts.note: the December 25 festival is a public holiday
Carol is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl takes a holiday in exchange for singing at the end of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Carols for the December festival are sung as the calendar closes.

clue.text: It may be a little snowy

definitions.text: It may be a little snowy

parts.words: It may be a little snowy
parts.note: 'snowy' reads as weather, but it names the white Arctic bird, and 'a little' one is its chick

explanation.definitionFit: A young bird of the snowy species is a small hooting chick.

clue.text: Emphatic refusal of credit by word of mouth?

definitions.meaning: British slang for hire purchase, buying on instalments

explanation.walkthrough: The 'never-never' is British slang for buying on hire purchase; 'by word of mouth' hints the refusal is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeating the word for 'not ever' is a firm no; the same phrase is slang for instalment buying.

clue.text: Pots of money are hidden inside a tower

indicators.note: the word are is concealed within the word for a fortune

parts.note: a mint is a large fortune, as in 'it cost a mint'
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stashes a fortune within a tower.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender mosque tower from which the call to prayer is made.

clue.text: Lamb trapped, for example, and caught — how sad

indicators.note: the pen name surrounds and holds the abbreviation for 'for example'

parts.note: Charles Lamb wrote his essays under the pen name Elia
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A lamb is trapped and caught, and someone sighs at how sad it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' looks like a young sheep, but it is the essayist Charles Lamb, whose pen name was Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac verse mourns, so the word means mournful or melancholy.

clue.text: In Athens, I make a very small amount

definitions.meaning: the Greek letter corresponding to our I

explanation.surface: A traveller in Greece claims to earn very little.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek alphabet's ninth letter is its smallest, hence a tiny scrap.

clue.text: How US 'responded to all English needs in the wars

indicators.note: a British idiom for knocked about or injured, so the letters are battered into a new order

explanation.surface: America answered every British need during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the wars' is British for battered and bruised. The scheme supplied Britain with arms and goods in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The wartime American programme supplied arms to Britain on loan terms.

clue.text: Sinister condition of Communist help sensed to be wrong

parts.note: communists are on the political left
to lend a hand is to help

indicators.note: the word sensed is put wrong, its letters muddled

explanation.surface: A communist senses that something is amiss in a sinister state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinister' is Latin for left, so the definition is a fair joke. 'To be wrong' rearranges SENSED into EDNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin sinister meant on the left side, so favouring that hand is a 'sinister condition'.

clue.text: Bearing left in unusually even race

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the jumbled letters
the words even race are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders what bearing a strangely even race has on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like posture or direction; here it means pertinence. 'Unusually' scrambles the two words, and 'in' places the abbreviation for left among them.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bearing on something is to be pertinent to it.

clue.text: Card is a joker?

definitions.meaning: to card wool is to comb out its fibres
someone who mocks or kids others

explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' looks like a playing card beside 'joker', but here it is the verb for combing wool, which can also be called teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Combing out wool fibres is carding, and a kidder who mocks playfully is a person given to ribbing.

clue.text: One making notes for Teacher without thanks

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the teacher's title surrounds the thanks

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone taking notes for the teacher gets no thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside here, not lacking. TA is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian stringed instrument produces musical notes.

clue.text: Bear didn't begin the destruction

indicators.note: the bear's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Bruin is a traditional name for a bear

explanation.surface: A bear is blamed for destruction it did not start.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin and destruction are synonyms for wreckage.

clue.text: Cried quietly in the rain

indicators.note: the musical letter for quietly is set inside the rainy word

parts.note: rain is wet weather, 'the wet'
p (piano) is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone sheds silent tears out in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: Shed tears, the past tense of weep.

clue.text: Not in favour of supporting mixed-up titled amateurs

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for against sits beneath, holding up the anagram
the word titled is mixed into a new order

parts.note: anti means opposed to

explanation.surface: Titled dabblers in a muddle get backing from those who oppose them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dabblers in the arts who lack professional commitment.

clue.text: Grace, giving an instant right impression

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
a dent is a hollow impression

explanation.surface: Grace grants a moment's honest impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grace' looks like a name or a virtue but means a grace note, a musical ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: A grace note ornament in music, a quick alternation with the note below.

clue.text: Write 'new directions for study on costume

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university
a dress is a costume or outfit

explanation.surface: An instruction to send fresh guidance about studying fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a fresh delivery location on an envelope or parcel.

clue.text: Could it make me rich? A fanciful idea!

indicators.note: the question asks whether these letters could be made into something new

explanation.surface: A dreamer wonders if a scheme will bring riches, then calls it fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could it make' rearranges ME RICH A.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical monster, by extension an illusory dream or wild fancy.

clue.text: Eight notes, then a semitone: that's unequally balanced for the triangle

parts.note: a musical scale runs over eight notes, an octave
read as semi-tone, half of the word tone, its second half

explanation.surface: A musical scale and a half-step make a lopsided triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Semitone' is read as half of TONE, giving NE. A scalene triangle has three unequal sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle with sides all different in length is lopsided in shape.

clue.text: Just loses it to get even

indicators.note: the word for fair drops the two letters of it

parts.note: equitable means fair or just

explanation.surface: A fair player loses and has to get even.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-tempered, calm and steady.

clue.text: Was terrified of looking like a Rastafarian?

definitions.meaning: wearing dreadlocks, the hairstyle linked to Rastafarians

explanation.definitionFit: Feared intensely; also wearing locks, the matted rope-like hair worn by Rastafarians.

clue.text: Let down by puncture

parts.note: reads as being disappointed, but describes a tyre losing its air through a hole

explanation.definitionFit: A punctured tyre loses air and goes flat.

clue.text: He helps in the rise of a comedian

indicators.note: the hidden letters are read upwards, backwards
the answer sits within the letters of comedian

explanation.surface: An assistant helps a comedian's career rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EDIA lies inside 'comedian'; 'the rise of' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant is someone who helps.

clue.text: Smack on the wrist

definitions.meaning: a light blow with the hand
the end of a sleeve, which sits at the wrist

explanation.surface: A parent gives a little slap on the wrist.
explanation.definitionFit: A light blow; also the band at the end of a sleeve.

clue.text: Where one comes to get bronzed?

definitions.text: Where one comes to get bronzed?

parts.words: Where one comes to get bronzed?
parts.note: 'bronzed' suggests a sunbed, but it means winning the bronze medal, which goes to the competitor finishing after gold and silver

explanation.definitionFit: Bronze medals go to the competitor who finishes behind gold and silver.

clue.text: I'm a success as a perfect butter, fly

parts.note: taken as written, losing its apostrophe
to make a go of something is to succeed

explanation.surface: Someone claims success as a perfect butter and then shoos a fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter, fly' hides 'butterfly': the definition is the perfect, adult insect, the final stage after the pupa.
explanation.definitionFit: Entomologists call the fully developed adult insect stage the perfect form.

clue.text: Dole out food, we hear

indicators.note: the word for food is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: meat is food

explanation.surface: Someone is said to dole out food.
explanation.definitionFit: To mete out is to allot or distribute.

clue.text: Honours even at first all round

parts.note: OBEs are British honours, Officers of the Order of the British Empire

indicators.note: only the opening letter of even is used

explanation.surface: Honours are shared evenly at the start for everyone around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All round' looks like an indicator but is the definition: very fat. The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossly overweight, so round in every direction.

clue.text: Bright idea, worth an alpha maybe?

definitions.meaning: an alpha is one kind of rhythm recorded from the head's electrical activity, so it counts as an example

explanation.definitionFit: A sudden clever thought; also an electrical rhythm of the brain, of which alpha is one type.

clue.text: Galahad took this investment, very risky

parts.note: investing a town means besieging it
perilous means dangerous

explanation.surface: A knight backs a dangerous financial venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial but means besieging. In Arthurian legend Galahad sat in the Round Table's perilous seat, fatal to anyone unworthy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Round Table's fatal seat which only the pure knight Galahad could occupy.
